question: What is the main cause of Tumor Lysis Syndrome when cancer treatment begins?

options.A: Rapid destruction of large numbers of cancer cells releasing contents into the blood
options.B: Bacterial invasion of the bloodstream due to low white blood cell counts
options.C: Severe dehydration caused by prolonged nausea and vomiting after chemotherapy
options.D: A sudden allergic reaction to the intravenous fluids administered in the clinic

explanation: You've got this! When chemo works *too* fast, cells burst open all at once, flooding the blood with waste products that stress the kidneys. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why is getting the community involved so important during an outbreak?

options.A: It ensures that international donors send financial aid instantly
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing or clinical staff
options.C: It completely stops the replication cycle of bacteria and viruses
options.D: It builds trust and prevents resistance or hiding of sick family members

explanation: When people trust nurses and understand what's going on, they cooperate openly and report sickness early instead of hiding it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why must instrument cleaning and brushing be done submerged under water?

options.A: To make the detergent foam up much faster
options.B: To prevent infectious droplets from splashing into the air
options.C: To cool down the metal before it gets handled
options.D: To save clean water from running out too quickly

explanation: Scrubbing in the open air creates fine mists that staff can inhale or that can contaminate surrounding sterile surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: What is the main job of the arachnoid granulations?

options.A: To supply strong structural support between skull bones
options.B: To allow cerebrospinal fluid to return to the venous blood
options.C: To manufacture fresh blood cells for the central nervous system
options.D: To anchor the spinal cord firmly to the vertebral column

explanation: You're doing great. These little structures act like drainage valves, letting used cerebrospinal fluid flow safely back into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T8#GNS211_U3_T8_h3)

question: When does intrapartum transmission of HIV primarily take place?

options.A: Through breast milk during the first week of life
options.B: As the baby passes through the birth canal
options.C: Across the placenta during the first trimester
options.D: Via airborne droplets in the delivery room

explanation: Intrapartum transmission happens when the infant is exposed to infected maternal blood and vaginal fluids during labor and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h2)

question: Why must you stay right by the patient during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules require physical presence to document vital signs
options.B: Most severe, life-threatening transfusion reactions occur during this initial window
options.C: Patients often feel lonely and anxious when receiving intravenous fluids
options.D: Pumps automatically lock out nurse access after fifteen minutes of running

explanation: Most bad reactions happen right at the beginning when the blood first hits circulation. Staying close lets you catch it instantly! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why is it important to ask if a patient has ever had surgery on their neck?

options.A: It can damage the thyroid or parathyroid glands
options.B: It stops the pancreas from producing insulin
options.C: It leads to chronic respiratory infections
options.D: It always causes permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Because the thyroid and parathyroid glands live right in the neck, past surgeries there can sometimes accidentally disrupt hormone control. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h5)

question: A midwife is reviewing a case where an embryo has successfully burrowed beneath the surface lining of the uterus. Which stage of implantation is this?

options.A: Cleavage
options.B: Invasion
options.C: Apposition
options.D: Adhesion

explanation: Brilliant! When the cells actively dig through the surface and sink into the womb lining, we call it invasion. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of multi-sectorial collaboration during a disaster?

options.A: To allow different agencies to work as a unified front
options.B: To let the health ministry manage all rescue operations
options.C: To reduce the total number of volunteers needed
options.D: To ensure only government agencies handle relief funds

explanation: Disasters require many different groups to combine their strengths so they can respond effectively together. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h1)

question: What is the emergency reversal drug given during a dangerous opioid overdose?

options.A: Protamine sulfate
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Naloxone is a lifesaver! It bumps opioids off their receptors in a hurry and helps the patient breathe again. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h6)

question: You ask a patient to touch their own nose and then touch your finger over and over. What are you testing?

options.A: Superficial pain perception
options.B: Cerebellar coordination
options.C: Cranial nerve vision
options.D: Deep tendon reflexes

explanation: The finger-to-nose test checks the cerebellum, which is the part of the brain that keeps your body movements smooth and coordinated. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential so vital in HIV nursing care?

options.A: Confidentiality laws prevent laboratories from processing viral load tests
options.B: Fear of social stigma often stops patients from seeking care or taking medications openly
options.C: Hospital management disciplines nurses who share room numbers with doctors
options.D: Uninsured patients will not pay their pharmacy bills if names are known

explanation: Spot on! Stigma is a huge barrier. Protecting privacy helps patients feel safe to come back for care and stick with their treatment. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h8)

question: When handling an emergency family planning complication, what extra communication duty does the nurse have?

options.A: Instructing the client to keep all information a secret
options.B: Posting the client's medical details on social media for donations
options.C: Calling or notifying the receiving facility in advance
options.D: Waiting for three days before writing the referral note

explanation: For urgent cases, advance communication ensures the receiving team prepares emergency equipment and bed space before arrival. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: What type of grief occurs before an actual loss takes place, such as during a terminal illness diagnosis?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Inhibitory grief
options.C: Complicated grief
options.D: Normal grief

explanation: Anticipatory grief starts before the actual loss happens as people process a pending terminal diagnosis. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which of these shows direct clinical competence during a nurse's evaluation?

options.A: The total number of personal phone calls made on duty
options.B: How well the nurse gets along with the hospital director
options.C: Correct medication administration technique
options.D: Whether the nurse wears fashionable shoes to work

explanation: Clinical competence is all about the actual nursing care you give. Getting your drug calculations and administration spot-on is a classic example! [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: What common economic challenge often forces families to rely heavily on cheap, refined carbohydrate meals?

options.A: A total lack of agricultural land for farming throughout the entire country
options.B: Financial poverty that makes fresh vegetables and lean proteins expensive
options.C: Universal free distribution of processed foods at primary healthcare centres
options.D: Strict government bans on importing nutritious food items into local markets

explanation: You've got it. Economic reality plays a huge role in health. When fresh protein and veggies are pricey, families naturally turn to cheaper, filling carbs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h7)

question: When is the right time for a nurse to document a medication?

options.A: Before pulling the medication from the dispensing cabinet
options.B: Right before walking into the patient hospital room
options.C: At the very end of the entire nursing shift
options.D: Immediately after the patient swallows or receives it

explanation: Exactly! Always chart right after giving meds. Doing it right away keeps your records accurate and stops another nurse from accidentally giving a double dose. [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community needs assessment in nursing?

options.A: Counting the total number of hospital beds available in the ward
options.B: Fulfilling administrative paperwork required by the local government council
options.C: Understanding what the community already knows, believes, and struggles with
options.D: Finding out which patients have enough money to pay private clinic fees

explanation: Well done! A needs assessment helps you find out the real gaps so your health teaching hits the right spot every time. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h3)

question: How does a 'diet' differ from a single 'food' item?

options.A: A diet is the total food and drink consumed over time, while a food is a single substance eaten.
options.B: A diet only includes liquids, while food only includes solids.
options.C: There is no difference between the two terms.
options.D: Foods are chemical compounds, while a diet is a medical prescription.

explanation: Think of food as an individual ingredient or meal, and diet as the whole picture of everything someone eats and drinks over time. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h2)

question: Why is 'modifiability' an important factor when deciding which health problem to tackle first?

options.A: It proves that chronic diseases are always easier to cure than acute infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for community participation in health planning
options.C: It guarantees that the local government will increase taxes for health programs
options.D: It ensures the team focuses on problems that can realistically be solved with available resources

explanation: Modifiability looks at whether an intervention can actually make a difference given current technology, funding, and staff capacity. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)

question: Two look-alike drug boxes on a pharmacy shelf led to a near-mixup. What is a great preventive action?

options.A: Punishing the nurse who collected the medication
options.B: Telling the pharmacist to be more careful without changing the shelves
options.C: Rearranging the pharmacy storage so those look-alike drugs are kept far apart
options.D: Stopping the purchase of all medications from that company

explanation: Spot on! Changing the physical setup removes the trap and stops future mix-ups before they start. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient data privacy rules in a digital hospital?

options.A: Sharing your computer login password with a fellow nurse who forgot theirs
options.B: Discussing a client's lab results inside a private consultation room
options.C: Reviewing the medical history of an assigned client during your shift
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record workstation before walking away

explanation: Never share your password! If someone else uses your login, you are responsible for any changes made in that patient's file. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of having both the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems working together?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal body balance
options.B: Preventing the brain from ever sleeping
options.C: Keeping the heart rate as high as possible
options.D: Ensuring constant physical exhaustion

explanation: Both systems balance each other out to achieve homeostasis—a fancy word for keeping your internal body happy, stable, and healthy. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T31#GNS211_U3_T31_h6)

question: A client calls the clinic to say she missed one active combination pill today. What should you advise her to do?

options.A: Take the missed pill immediately and continue as normal
options.B: Wait until tomorrow and take three pills at once
options.C: Throw away the rest of the month and start a new pack
options.D: Stop taking the pack entirely and wait for her next menses

explanation: Don't panic over one missed pill! Just take the forgotten pill right away and keep going with your normal schedule to stay protected. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h2)

question: Where is the best place on the body to give an emergency intramuscular shot of epinephrine?

options.A: Dorsal gluteal muscle
options.B: Anterolateral thigh
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Subcutaneous abdominal fat

explanation: Spot on! The outer-front part of the thigh (anterolateral thigh) absorbs medications into the bloodstream much faster and more reliably than other sites. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a community health nurse would focus on during an IDP camp assessment?

options.A: Environmental waste and refuse disposal sites
options.B: Private stock market investment portfolios
options.C: Availability and safety of drinking water
options.D: Presence of vulnerable pregnant women and infants

explanation: Nurses focus on health, safety, and sanitation needs—not financial investments! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h3)

question: Which type of synovial joint gives you the biggest range of movement in all directions?

options.A: Hinge joint
options.B: Pivot joint
options.C: Plane joint
options.D: Ball-and-socket joint

explanation: That's right! Your shoulders and hips are ball-and-socket joints, allowing you to swing your arms and legs in almost any direction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is it so helpful to teach elderly patients with chronic illnesses how to monitor themselves?

options.A: It helps catch worsening symptoms early before emergency care is needed.
options.B: It eliminates all normal age-related physical decline.
options.C: It completely removes the need for regular nursing home visits.
options.D: It allows the patient to change their prescription dosages alone.

explanation: You nailed it! When patients keep an eye on their own warning signs, little issues get caught early—long before they turn into scary hospital emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the biggest weakness of using the rational (logical) method by itself?

options.A: It cannot be written down on paper or spoken aloud
options.B: It ignores all forms of mathematical calculation
options.C: A flawed starting premise leads to an incorrect conclusion
options.D: It takes too many years to complete a single calculation

explanation: Logic is only as good as its starting point. If your first assumption is wrong, your final answer will be wrong too! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h5)

question: An elderly patient gets too tired halfway through meals and leaves most food. What should you suggest?

options.A: Force the patient to finish everything on the plate
options.B: Serve smaller, more frequent meals throughout the day
options.C: Wait until the patient asks for food days later
options.D: Stop offering solid food and start tube feeding

explanation: Great thinking! Smaller portions prevent fatigue and help weak patients eat enough total calories. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h6)

question: What type of care approach is most effective when treating survivors of forced marriage?

options.A: Experimental surgical care
options.B: Strictly punitive care
options.C: Cosmetic dermatological care
options.D: Trauma-informed care

explanation: Trauma-informed care acknowledges the profound psychological impact of abuse and focuses on safety, trust, and empowerment for the survivor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h7)

question: How does a receptor antagonist antidote work to reverse an overdose?

options.A: It binds to heavy metals and flushes them out through the urine
options.B: It attaches to the same cell sites as the poison to block its action
options.C: It coats the lining of the stomach so the poison cannot pass through
options.D: It destroys the chemical structure of the poison inside the blood

explanation: Think of it like musical chairs! The antagonist rushes in and sits on the cell receptors first, blocking the poison from grabbing a seat and doing damage. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which sign strongly suggests internal bleeding in a patient on blood thinners?

options.A: Complaints of severe itching on the arms and legs
options.B: A sudden rise in the patient's body temperature
options.C: An increase in urine output over twenty-four hours
options.D: The presence of dark, tarry stools in the bedpan

question: On a partograph, what does it mean if labour progress crosses the "alert line"?

options.A: Labour is progressing slowly and requires closer observation
options.B: Immediate surgical delivery is mandatory right this second
options.C: The baby has already been successfully delivered
options.D: The mother's blood pressure is completely normal

question: When do you check the Apgar score for a newborn baby?

options.A: At birth and every ten minutes
options.B: At one and five minutes after birth
options.C: At thirty minutes and one hour
options.D: At five and fifteen minutes after birth

explanation: You got this! We check the Apgar score right at 1 minute and 5 minutes of life. This helps us see how well the baby is adjusting to breathing on their own outside the womb. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to pour household cleaning chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: Bottled drinks cannot hold the weight of heavy industrial-strength soap

options.C: The plastic material used in beverage bottles reacts poorly with standard water
options.D: It increases the risk of accidental ingestion by mistaking the chemical for a drink

question: What is a major reason farm crops get wasted before they ever reach the market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in local supermarkets
options.B: Poor storage facilities and inadequate transport networks
options.C: Immediate consumption of all crops by farmers
options.D: Strict government laws against selling fresh crops

explanation: Bad roads and lack of proper storage silos mean harvested food often spoils before getting to people who need it. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h2)

question: What can you find living inside a mature parasitic egg?

options.A: Free-floating viral particles
options.B: An adult reproducing worm
options.C: Active bacterial colonies
options.D: A fully formed or developing larva

explanation: Depending on how mature it is, the egg holds either early cells or a fully ready-to-hatch larva. You're crushing it! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is a common long-term effect of eating too many trans and saturated fats?

options.A: Atherosclerosis and higher heart risk
options.B: Stronger storage of vitamins in bones
options.C: Less inflammation in the arteries
options.D: Better production of good cholesterol

question: What is the biggest benefit of standardizing nursing workflows on the ward?

options.A: To increase the amount of daily paperwork required
options.B: To make clinical actions predictable and reduce cognitive load
options.C: To eliminate the need for physician orders in emergencies
options.D: To ensure all nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Standardization creates a comforting routine. When tasks are done the same way across the unit, you don't have to overthink every little step, freeing up your brain for patient care! [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h4)

question: When nurses are faced with multiple community health problems, which factor helps them decide which to tackle first?

options.A: Color of the local clinic building
options.B: Number of desks in the health office
options.C: Magnitude and severity of the problem
options.D: Personal preference of the junior nurse

question: Why must the antiseptic skin prep dry completely before the needle enters?

question: A patient from a fishing community presents with blood in their urine and lower belly pain. Which parasite is the likely cause?

options.A: Necator americanus
options.B: Enterobius vermicularis
options.C: Schistosoma species
options.D: Ascaris lumbricoides

question: How can bedside nurses help lower overall health care costs?

options.A: By preventing hospital-acquired complications and minimizing supply waste
options.B: By charging patients directly for bedside nursing procedures
options.C: By eliminating all diagnostic tests from patient care plans
options.D: By shortening physician consultation times during emergencies

explanation: Stopping problems like pressure sores or infections keeps patients safe, out of intensive care, and saves money on wasted supplies. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h7)

question: In Nigeria's routine immunization schedule, which vaccines are given right at birth?

options.A: Measles 1, Yellow Fever, and Meningitis

question: What is the primary purpose of presenting data in nursing research?

options.A: To make raw information easy to understand and use
options.B: To replace the need for written conclusions
options.C: To make research articles longer and more academic
options.D: To hide errors in clinical measurements

explanation: Presenting data organizes chaotic raw information into a clear format so readers can easily grasp clinical findings. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h1)

question: What happens to the airways in your lungs when the sympathetic nervous system kicks in?

options.A: Complete airway closure
options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Bronchoconstriction
options.D: Increased mucus secretion

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward

options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

question: A patient complains that constant hospital noise and glaring overhead lights won't let them sleep. What kind of stressor is this?

options.A: Environmental stressor
options.B: Eustress
options.C: Psychosocial stressor
options.D: Physiological stressor

explanation: Things around us in our physical surroundings—like annoying hospital sounds or bright lights—are environmental stressors. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is the main focus of client-centered drug administration?

options.A: Following hospital medication schedules without exception
options.B: Leaving medication management entirely to the doctor
options.C: Reducing the time nurses spend talking to patients
options.D: Treating the patient as an active partner in their care

explanation: Client-centered care values the patient's active participation in their own treatment plan rather than treating them as a passive recipient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main reason we give food to a patient in the hospital?

options.A: To test the kitchen staff's ability to prepare local dishes
options.B: To keep the patient occupied during hospital visiting hours
options.C: To yield energy, build tissue, and regulate processes
options.D: To lower the total cost of hospital admission fees

question: What is the main purpose of a feedback slip in the referral process?

options.A: To notify the primary clinic about the outcome of the client's visit

options.C: To serve as a receipt for hospital treatment fees paid by the client
options.D: To record the daily attendance of nurses at the tertiary hospital

explanation: The feedback slip is like a reply letter! It travels back from the big hospital to tell your clinic what treatment was given. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient on long-term warfarin who loves green leafy vegetables?

options.A: Stop eating all green vegetables immediately to stay safe
options.B: Double your vegetable intake only on days you take extra medication
options.C: Eat a consistent amount of green vegetables every week without sudden big changes
options.D: Boil all green vegetables for two hours to destroy all vitamins

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended for women after childbirth?

options.A: To strengthen muscles and prevent urinary incontinence
options.B: To increase the total volume of breastmilk produced
options.C: To help tighten abdominal skin after a C-section
options.D: To accelerate the growth of the newborn's bones

question: A community experiences a sudden outbreak of severe diarrhea linked to contaminated street food. What is the most appropriate regulatory response?

options.A: Blame consumers for choosing to eat outside their homes

options.C: Inspect food handling practices and provide hygiene education to vendors
options.D: Ban the sale of all food items in the entire country permanently

question: Why is strict waste segregation vital during home visits?

options.D: It reduces the total weight of the home visiting kit bag

question: Which diagnostic test directly checks the strength and status of a patient's immune system?

options.C: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.D: Liver enzyme panel

question: What special type of room ventilation is a must-have for patients on airborne precautions?

options.A: Positive pressure room
options.B: Standard natural ventilation room
options.C: Negative pressure room
options.D: Reverse isolation airflow room

question: What is another common name for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Cerebral shunt
options.B: Spinal tap
options.C: Epidural injection

question: What is the main focus of the 'preparedness' phase in disaster management?

options.A: Providing immediate search and rescue operations during an active earthquake

options.C: Rebuilding damaged roads and bridges months after floodwaters recede
options.D: Building operational readiness and planning before a disaster strikes

explanation: Preparedness always happens before the storm. It is all about running drills, stocking supplies, and getting your team ready so you are never caught off guard. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using a guide like the Iowa Model in nursing?

options.A: To punish nurses who refuse to follow new guidelines

options.C: To help researchers write better scientific articles
options.D: To provide a step-by-step roadmap for making clinical changes

explanation: Well done! Models like the Iowa Model give us a clear, friendly roadmap to follow from the moment we spot a problem to when we check if our change worked. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h3)

question: What kind of drug is misoprostol?

options.A: A selective progesterone receptor modulator
options.B: A synthetic prostaglandin E1 analogue
options.C: A long-acting synthetic estrogen derivative
options.D: A beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist

question: Why is involving family members in dietary education so important for these patients?

options.A: Family members usually buy and prepare the food eaten at home
options.B: The family is legally responsible if the patient breaks the diet
options.C: Relatives must also follow a strict low protein diet together
options.D: It prevents the patient from cooking hot meals on the stove

explanation: Because household food preparation is often a shared or family duty, involving relatives ensures the prescribed diet is actually followed at home. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h6)

question: Why do nurses use a pH testing strip when checking a newly placed nasogastric tube?

options.A: To test how acidic the fluid pulled from the tube is
options.B: To check the expiry date of the food formula
options.C: To check if the patient has a stomach ulcer
options.D: To measure the sugar level in the feed

explanation: Stomach acid is very sour! Testing the pH of fluid from the tube helps us confirm the tip is safely inside the acidic stomach, not the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h3)

question: When handing over a critical patient, what does the acronym SBAR stand for?

options.A: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Airway, Respiration
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: System, Burden, Action, Review

explanation: SBAR is your best friend for smooth handovers. Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation keeps everything short, sweet, and safe! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of open-access academic journals?

options.A: Articles are published overnight without any editorial oversight
options.B: Practitioners worldwide can read the findings without paying expensive fees
options.C: Studies are automatically approved for funding by the health ministry
options.D: Researchers never have to revise their original drafts or fix errors

explanation: Open-access removes paywalls so that nurses and the public can freely access vital health information. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h2)

question: In healthcare, what does the term 'pharmacovigilance' mean?

options.A: Monitoring and studying adverse drug reactions and safety issues
options.B: Manufacturing synthetic drugs in sterile laboratory environments
options.C: Setting international market prices for essential pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Inspecting local pharmacies for expired prescription medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance simply means keeping a watchful eye on medications to catch, study, and prevent any harmful side effects. You're building great clinical vocabulary! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary benefit of peer support groups for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Learning advanced medical surgical nursing procedures
options.B: Finding government-funded employment without interviews
options.C: Connecting with others who share similar experiences and offer practical advice
options.D: Receiving free prescription medications and medical supplies

explanation: Peer support reduces isolation and gives individuals hope by seeing others successfully navigate similar life challenges. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h6)

question: What is the best way to confirm a family caregiver actually knows how to manage a feeding tube?

options.A: Ask if they understood the instructions given
options.B: Give the caregiver a written quiz on medical terms
options.C: Ask the caregiver to demonstrate the skill back to the nurse
options.D: Check if they bought the required equipment

question: An older resident taking blood pressure pills suddenly feels dizzy and takes a fall. What should the nurse think of first?

options.A: An immediate need to discharge the resident home.
options.B: The complete absence of any pharmacological influence.
options.C: A normal reaction that requires no clinical follow-up.
options.D: A potential adverse drug reaction or cumulative medication effect.

explanation: Dizziness and sudden falls in older adults are classic clues that a medication might be lowering their blood pressure too much or making them drowsy. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: During the active phase of the first stage of labour, how often should you listen to the baby's heart rate?

options.A: Every 30 minutes
options.B: Only after membranes rupture
options.C: Every 2 hours
options.D: Every 5 minutes

explanation: Keep it up! Checking the fetal heart rate every 30 minutes helps you catch any signs of distress early and keep both mom and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h4)

question: What does a high amount of out-of-pocket health spending usually tell us about a country?

options.A: A weak public financial safety net for citizens
options.B: An exceptionally strong and free healthcare system
options.C: That citizens pay very low taxes overall
options.D: That the government is meeting all international health targets

explanation: When patients have to pay cash for almost everything at the hospital, it usually means the government's safety net isn't quite covering them yet. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which type of adverse drug reaction is totally predictable because it depends directly on the dose?

options.A: Idiosyncratic reaction
options.B: Type A reaction
options.C: Type B reaction
options.D: Allergic reaction

explanation: Type A reactions happen because the drug's normal action is just too strong. Because they are dose-related, they are easy to predict! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a social, political, or cultural factor that affects food access?

options.A: The daily weather temperature and rainfall volume
options.B: Political conflict that disrupts food transport
options.C: Cultural traditions regarding who eats first in a household
options.D: Land distribution laws that affect local farmers

explanation: Weather and rain are natural or environmental factors, while the others are human-made, social, or political elements. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h6)

question: What does the presence of *Escherichia coli* in a well water sample indicate?

options.A: Recent fecal contamination from warm-blooded animals
options.B: High concentration of dissolved iron minerals
options.C: Natural mineral runoff from nearby rocks
options.D: Exposed electrical wiring inside the pump

explanation: E. coli lives primarily in animal and human guts, so finding it in water proves that waste matter has entered the source. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for remodeling collagen and softening ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Relaxin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol

explanation: Relaxin is produced during pregnancy to soften ligaments and joints, preparing the pelvis for delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: What is the typical chemical structure of a dietary fat (triglyceride)?

options.A: Four interlocking carbon rings with a side chain
options.B: One nitrogen group attached to a central carbon ring
options.C: Two sugar rings joined by a strong glycosidic bond
options.D: One glycerol molecule attached to three fatty acid tails

question: Why is being decisive so important during a sudden medical emergency on the ward?

options.A: It stops doctors from entering the patient's room.
options.B: It provides clear direction and reassures the team.
options.C: It guarantees that no equipment will ever break down.
options.D: It ensures the nurse manager avoids doing paperwork.

explanation: When panic threatens to take over during an emergency, clear and calm instructions from a decisive leader bring order and help save lives. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a major reason doctors prescribe corticosteroids for lung conditions?

options.A: To thin thick mucus so coughing is easier
options.B: To reduce airway swelling during severe asthma attacks
options.C: To kill bacterial germs inside the lungs
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in lung vessels

explanation: Well done! Steroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs that quickly open up swollen airways when an asthma attack strikes. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why must calcium bind to troponin before a muscle can contract?

options.A: It directly provides the energy needed for the power stroke
options.B: It moves tropomyosin away from actin binding sites
options.C: It holds the Z-lines firmly in place during movement
options.D: It destroys excess acetylcholine in the synapse

explanation: At rest, tropomyosin blocks the binding sites like a locked door. Calcium acts as the key that shifts it out of the way so the muscle can get to work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: What does the term polyuria mean in a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Severe pain and burning sensation during urination
options.B: Excessive production and passing of urine
options.C: A sudden and total inability to pass any urine
options.D: An intense, constant craving for sweet foods

explanation: Polyuria refers to passing large volumes of urine, which happens when excess sugar pulls extra water out of the body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: What does juvenile delinquency mean?

options.A: Severe mental illness manifesting during early adolescent years
options.B: Disobedient behavior shown exclusively within a school environment

options.D: Minor disobedience corrected entirely through parental discipline

question: Why does Primary Health Care require different sectors to work together (intersectoral collaboration)?

options.A: Because the Ministry of Health cannot legally purchase medications without other ministries

options.C: Because health is influenced by non-medical factors like education, agriculture, and clean water
options.D: Because nurses are required to work in agricultural fields during planting seasons

explanation: Well done! Good health goes beyond medicine. It relies heavily on food security, safe water, and education—which means different government sectors must team up. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why does parental apathy pose a serious problem for the PTA?

options.A: It forces the government to close down all private hospitals
options.B: It automatically increases the academic salaries of teachers
options.C: It leads to poor attendance and lack of support for school programs
options.D: It stops students from participating in sports competitions

question: Why is the immune system called a 'diffuse' system instead of just one single organ?

options.A: It relies entirely on the brain to direct every defensive action
options.B: It only functions when a person is actively sleeping or resting
options.C: It changes its physical structure completely every few days
options.D: It consists of cells, tissues, and organs spread throughout the body

question: Which of these common substances acts as a Central Nervous System (CNS) depressant?

options.A: Amphetamine
options.B: Nicotine
options.C: Alcohol
options.D: Cocaine

explanation: Correct! Alcohol slows down brain activity, making it a depressant. Remember: depressants slow things down, while stimulants speed them up. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why might a newly graduated nurse hesitate to accept delegated duties from a senior colleague?

options.A: Fear of failure and lack of professional self-confidence
options.B: Belief that delegation is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Desire to take over the senior colleague's official management title
options.D: Preference for administrative paperwork over direct patient care

explanation: It's totally normal for fresh grads to feel nervous! Doubts usually stem from a lack of confidence and the fear of making mistakes early on. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why are community health programs that teach about local crops so effective at preventing disease?

options.A: They replace the human need for macronutrients
options.B: They empower communities to use accessible foods to stay healthy
options.C: They rely entirely on expensive imported medications
options.D: They eliminate the need for any clinical healthcare workers

explanation: Exactly! Teaching people how to make the best of what's already growing around them builds long-lasting, self-reliant health habits. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h5)

question: You see a toddler running around the living room while eating crackers. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait until the child finishes running to intervene.

options.C: Calmly ask the child to sit at the table before eating more.

question: Why do quality improvement experts focus on fixing systems instead of blaming individual nurses when mistakes happen?

options.A: Because clinical systems are structured to produce the exact results they currently deliver

options.C: Because individual staff members never make mistakes during busy shifts

question: According to the Frank-Starling law, what happens when more blood returns to the heart?

question: What is the main goal of teaching a family home care after treating a patient for head lice?

options.C: To force the family to cut their hair short for safety

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pregnant women are legally required to visit the clinic every single week

options.C: Clinics require attendance records to secure international funding
options.D: Dangerous conditions like high blood pressure can develop without early warning signs

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.C: To provide a direct connection to the external urinary meatus

question: Why is complete chest recoil important between compressions?

options.B: It gives the rescuer a chance to rest their arms

question: What is the main benefit of using hydrotherapy (water exercise) in rehab?

options.C: It eliminates all risks of secondary skin infections.
options.D: It completely cures chronic neurological disorders in days.

question: A patient hasn't been able to hit their strict diet targets over the past month. What should you do?

options.C: Scold the patient for failing to follow professional medical advice

question: An administrator says 'no' to your staffing proposal because it costs too much. What is your best next move?

question: How does a joint venture differ from standard facility outsourcing?

question: A patient with severe physical trauma from a motor vehicle accident is admitted to the ward. How does this physiological state affect their nutritional needs?

options.A: Metabolic demand increases, requiring more nutrients to prevent breakdown
options.B: Vitamins and minerals are no longer needed during acute healing
options.C: Water intake should be restricted to prevent cellular swelling
options.D: Caloric needs drop significantly because the patient is lying in bed

question: A patient asks why her body doesn't reject the developing pregnancy as a foreign object. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The baby carries the exact same blood type as the mother always

options.C: The mother's immune system shuts down completely during pregnancy

question: What kind of flavor experience does the umami taste sensation give us?

options.A: The biological indicator for sugars

options.D: The sharp warning signal of acids

question: Which essential vitamin is manufactured by the friendly bacteria living in our large intestine?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin K
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Vitamin D

question: As a student nurse, what is your main personal duty when it comes to hospital waste guidelines?

options.A: To prosecute scavengers who enter hospital grounds
options.B: To manufacture color-coded waste bags for the facility
options.C: To comply with disposal protocols and protect patients and staff from hazards
options.D: To design the hospital's waste incinerator plant

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital when nursing adolescent patients?

options.A: It builds trust and prevents teenagers from hiding important health details
options.B: It reduces the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily
options.C: It allows teenagers to prescribe their own medications safely
options.D: It is required by law so parents never have to speak to doctors

explanation: Young people need to know their secrets are safe so they feel secure enough to share honest health concerns. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which vital sign change usually comes with a widespread inflammatory response?

question: Why is oxytocin given right after a baby is delivered?

options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix

question: Which of the '5 Rs' motivational counseling steps helps a patient spot personal barriers and challenges to quitting?

options.A: Rewards
options.B: Roadblocks
options.C: Relevance
options.D: Risks

question: Which of these is an effective strategy nurses use to prevent medication errors?

options.D: Double-check verification processes for high-alert drugs

question: What is performance-based financing in healthcare?

options.A: Paying hospital workers a fixed salary regardless of patient volume
options.B: Rewarding health facilities based on achieved health targets and outputs
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign loans to pay medical staff
options.D: Giving free money to hospitals without any auditing

question: What is the first practical step a person should take when starting a weekly meal plan?

options.A: Visiting the local market without a list

options.D: Checking current pantry and refrigerator inventory

question: What do we call a patient who keeps shedding germs even after they've started feeling better?

options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Acute clinical case
options.D: Convalescent carrier

question: What is the main goal of 'pharmacovigilance' in healthcare?

options.C: To lower the financial cost of purchasing new prescription medicines

question: What is the main reason we incubate a clinical sample in the lab?

options.A: To remove all liquid content from the collected patient swab

options.C: To preserve the sample indefinitely without any chemical changes

question: What should a nurse do FIRST when an Alzheimer's patient suddenly becomes aggressive?

options.C: Scold the patient firmly to stop the unacceptable behavior

question: What is the main point of the evaluation phase in your care plan?

options.C: To write a formal letter of discharge for the patient's family

question: What type of computer is the bedside tablet you use for clinical charting?

options.D: Analog processor

question: What makes spinal nerves classified as mixed nerves?

options.D: They carry both sensory and motor signals

question: Why is it a big mistake to submerge an infrared thermometer in cleaning liquid?

options.C: It dissolves the outer plastic casing instantly
options.D: It turns the digital display screen permanently black

explanation: Liquid leaking inside will short-circuit the board and mess up the sensitive sensors. Always wipe, never soak! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h7)

question: How does nursing care in a half-way house differ from an acute hospital ward?

options.A: It focuses on rehabilitation, education, and community reintegration
options.B: It requires nurses to diagnose patients without a doctor present
options.C: It forbids nurses from talking to patients about their feelings
options.D: It relies entirely on physical restraints and locked isolation cells

explanation: Correct! Instead of dealing with emergency crises, residential nursing is all about teaching coping skills, guiding rehabilitation, and helping patients reconnect with society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h6)

question: A community health nurse in a Nigerian riverine village wants to run a program against paragonimiasis. What should be the top priority?

options.A: Screening pregnant mothers for gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Holding health talks on safe food preparation by local rivers
options.C: Distributing mosquito nets to all households in the community
options.D: Administering routine oral polio vaccines to infants

explanation: Brilliant choice! Focusing on local dietary habits and safe cooking directly targets how the infection is actually spread in that community. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h8)

question: Which of the following is an example of a wearable health device?

options.A: A smartwatch that tracks daily heart rate and step counts
options.B: A paper logbook kept inside a bedside medical trolley
options.C: A large desktop computer in the hospital billing office
options.D: A wall-mounted thermometer in the nurse's station

explanation: Wearable devices are worn on the body by the user to monitor health metrics continuously. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which finding during a routine IV assessment suggests the dressing needs immediate replacement?

options.A: The intravenous fluid bag is half full of normal saline
options.B: The patient reports sleeping well through the entire night
options.C: The dressing edges are lifting and exposing the insertion site
options.D: The extension tubing is coiled neatly on the bed sheet

explanation: Lifting dressings lose their sterile seal, increasing the risk of bacteria entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of using a problem tree analysis in community health?

options.A: To map out the geographical boundaries of a farming community
options.B: To measure the exact height and weight of growing children
options.C: To trace visible symptoms back to their underlying root causes
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of buying medical drugs

explanation: A problem tree helps health workers look past surface symptoms to find the true core cause of a health issue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: Why are Infant Welfare Clinics usually set up right inside primary health care centres?

options.A: To provide specialized pediatric surgery units
options.B: To isolate sick children from the general population
options.C: To bring preventive services closer to local communities
options.D: To reduce the workload of tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Placing clinics in local primary health care centres brings essential services right to the grassroots, making it super easy for families to attend routine check-ups. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h1)

question: Why is leprosy treated with a mix of different drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To cut out the need for blood tests
options.B: To heal skin sores overnight
options.C: To stop the bacteria from becoming resistant to the drugs
options.D: To make the treatment cheaper to buy

explanation: Using a combination of medications ensures the smart little germs can't mutate and outsmart a single drug. Brilliant concept to know! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which drug class is commonly used to help with burning or shooting nerve pain?

options.A: Antacids
options.B: Blood thinners
options.C: Anticonvulsants
options.D: Loop diuretics

explanation: Anticonvulsants (normally used for seizures) calm down jittery, overactive nerves that cause sharp, burning nerve pain. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h5)

question: How do peptide and protein hormones typically travel through the bloodstream?

options.A: They require specialized carrier proteins to move through blood
options.B: They precipitate out of solution if not bound to electrolytes
options.C: They are water-soluble and dissolve freely in blood plasma
options.D: They are fat-soluble and travel inside red blood cells

explanation: Because protein and peptide hormones love water, they dissolve easily right into the watery plasma of your blood and swim along freely without needing a special ride. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why must sharps segregation happen immediately at the point of origin?

options.A: To make the sharps box heavier so it does not tip over
options.B: To comply with local fashion trends in hospital design
options.C: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries during transport
options.D: To ensure the needles can be washed and reused later

explanation: Throwing needles directly into a nearby puncture-proof container stops nurses and cleaners from getting stuck while moving loose sharps later. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary job of the hormone relaxin during pregnancy?

options.A: To loosen ligaments and joints, especially in the pelvis
options.B: To calm the digestive tract and reduce morning sickness
options.C: To soften the amniotic sac and prevent premature rupture
options.D: To relax the airways and improve maternal oxygen intake

explanation: Relaxin lives up to its name! It relaxes and softens the body's connective tissues to get the pelvis ready for the baby to pass through during birth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h6)

question: Why are dietary fats considered energy-dense?

options.A: They contain no carbon or hydrogen atoms
options.B: They convert directly into muscle without breakdown
options.C: They are digested much faster than carbs
options.D: They supply more than double the calories per gram compared to carbs or protein

explanation: You've got this! Fats give you nine calories per gram, while proteins and carbs only give four. That means fats pack much more energy into a smaller amount. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: When is a patient officially diagnosed with epilepsy?

options.A: After a single unprovoked seizure occurs
options.B: Whenever an abnormal EEG result is recorded
options.C: When a patient has a high fever with shaking
options.D: After two or more unprovoked seizures

explanation: Spot on! Doctors look for a pattern before diagnosing epilepsy—specifically, having two or more seizures that weren't triggered by an obvious cause like a high fever. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why do laboratories test for indicator organisms instead of every pathogen?

options.A: Indicator bacteria neutralize all other chemical toxins
options.B: Pathogens cannot survive long enough to be detected in labs
options.C: Testing for every single pathogen is too difficult and expensive
options.D: Indicator organisms are the only microbes that cause illness

explanation: Pathogens are numerous and hard to isolate individually, so checking for reliable indicators is faster and more practical. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h5)

question: When is it safe to upgrade a patient from clear fluids to full fluids?

options.A: Immediately upon admission before any assessment occurs
options.B: When the patient demands solid meat and fibrous vegetables
options.C: When the patient tolerates clear fluids without nausea or cramping
options.D: When the patient develops severe diarrhea from dairy products

explanation: We step things up gradually. If their tummy handles clear fluids well without vomiting or cramps, they are ready for the next level! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h3)

question: A postoperative patient refuses to eat because food always brings severe belly pain and nausea. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Administer prescribed pain and anti-nausea medications thirty minutes before the next meal
options.B: Remove all food trays permanently and start total parenteral nutrition
options.C: Force the patient to finish the entire meal tray immediately
options.D: Tell the patient that eating is mandatory for legal discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Managing pain and nausea before mealtime makes eating comfortable so the patient can actually get their nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h8)

question: Why do different agencies need to work together during a disaster response?

options.A: It gives nurses the authority to write new national laws
options.B: It replaces the need for community education and local drills
options.C: It guarantees that natural hazards will completely miss the country
options.D: It ensures that different groups do not duplicate efforts and waste resources

explanation: Brilliant! Sharing information and working hand-in-hand prevents confusion and keeps help running smoothly. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h7)

question: During which stage of an infection does a patient first feel generally 'off' with vague, mild fatigue?

options.A: The convalescent stage
options.B: The illness stage
options.C: The prodromal stage
options.D: The incubation period

explanation: The prodromal stage is that tricky early window where a patient just feels mildly tired or has a low-grade fever before the main symptoms show up. [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of antimicrobial stewardship programs in hospitals?

options.A: Lowering hospital cleaning budgets by reducing soap purchases
options.B: Optimizing the use of anti-infectives to reduce resistance and harm
options.C: Ensuring every patient receives intravenous drugs automatically
options.D: Eliminating the need for laboratory cultures completely

explanation: Antimicrobial stewardship is all about using the right drug, at the right dose, for the right time—protecting patients from side effects and stopping superbugs from forming. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is one of the biggest perks for a patient joining a disease-specific support group?

options.A: It replaces the need for professional medical consultations
options.B: It reduces feelings of isolation by connecting people with similar challenges
options.C: It completely stops the progression of the degenerative disease
options.D: It provides financial compensation for medical bills

explanation: Support groups remind patients and families that they are never walking this difficult road alone. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h5)

question: How should you talk to a patient who has trouble hearing?

options.A: Shout loudly so the sound travels across the room
options.B: Whisper quietly directly into the patient's ear
options.C: Face the patient directly and speak in a normal tone
options.D: Use complex medical terms written on a notepad

explanation: Shouting actually distorts your words and makes lip-reading harder. Face them directly, speak clearly at a normal volume, and minimize background noise. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why do doctors order an MRI when they suspect a neurodegenerative disease?

options.A: To directly count the number of living neurons
options.B: To cure abnormal protein accumulation
options.C: To visualize brain structures and rule out other causes
options.D: To measure electrical brain waves

explanation: An MRI gives a clear picture of the brain so doctors can check for things like strokes or tumors that might look like a degenerative disease. Smart nursing insight! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is knowing the exact route abbreviation so important for safe medication delivery?

options.A: It determines how fast the drug works and prevents wrong-route errors
options.B: It replaces the need to check the patient's identity band
options.C: It decides which nurse is legally permitted to touch the patient
options.D: It tells the nurse the exact financial cost of the medication supply

explanation: Spot on! Different routes change how quickly a drug enters the bloodstream. Getting the route wrong can lead to serious patient harm, so always double-check! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is it so important to make sure a new mother passes urine early after birth?

options.A: To prepare her for immediate discharge home
options.B: To prove that she is drinking enough herbal teas
options.C: To prevent bladder distension which can cause uterine atony and hemorrhage
options.D: To calculate the exact amount of daily calories she burns

explanation: Brilliant! If the bladder gets too full, it pushes the uterus out of place, stopping it from contracting tightly and opening the door for heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h4)

question: Before checking an adult patient's height with a stadiometer, what must the nurse ask them to do first?

options.A: If the room temperature is comfortable for the patient
options.B: Whether the patient can hold their breath during the measurement
options.C: If the patient has eaten a large meal within the last two hours
options.D: Whether the patient has removed their shoes and heavy outer clothing

explanation: Spot on! Shoes, caps, and bulky jackets add extra height, so taking them off ensures your reading is true. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h3)

question: Two senior nurses are arguing bitterly over shift schedules, and the manager encourages both to give up a preferred off-day to meet in the middle. Which style is this?

options.A: Avoiding
options.B: Competing
options.C: Compromise
options.D: Collaboration

explanation: Compromise requires each person to concede something, resulting in a shared middle ground where neither gets everything they wanted. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h7)

question: Which model looks at behaviour change as stepping through different stages, like thinking about it, then finally taking action?

options.A: Transtheoretical Model
options.B: Epidemiological Triangle
options.C: Health Belief Model
options.D: Germ Theory of Disease

explanation: Spot on! The Transtheoretical Model helps us understand that change takes time and happens in steady steps. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h2)

question: In maritime healthcare, what does the abbreviation TMAS stand for?

options.A: Transport Medical Action System
options.B: Trauma Management At Sea
options.C: Total Maritime Air Support
options.D: Telemedical Assistance Service

explanation: You got it! TMAS connects ships at sea with land-based medical experts for remote guidance and advice. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h5)

question: What does the term group dynamics refer to in a healthcare setting?

options.A: The official administrative hierarchy of the hospital
options.B: The physical layout of equipment in the clinic ward
options.C: The changing behaviors and interactions within a team
options.D: The total number of patients treated in a single day

explanation: Group dynamics describes how members of a group relate, behave, and influence each other while working toward a goal. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which hospital team member is usually your go-to expert for helping a discharged patient find housing and food support?

options.A: The psychiatric social worker
options.B: The surgical floor pharmacist
options.C: The hospital laboratory technician
options.D: The institutional chief accountant

explanation: Spot on! Social workers are pros at connecting patients with community support, government programs, and welfare resources. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the best lab sample to take when checking for a polio infection?

options.A: Sputum sample
options.B: Blood culture
options.C: Urine sample
options.D: Stool sample

explanation: You nailed it! Since the virus multiplies happily in the gut, stool samples are the most reliable way for the lab to find it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h3)

question: What crucial detail must you write on a newly mixed (reconstituted) suspension bottle?

options.A: The patient's room number and diagnosis
options.B: The exact date and time the medication expires
options.C: The name of the pharmacy supplier
options.D: The manufacturer's original stock number

explanation: Always label your mixtures! Reconstituted drugs spoil fast once water is added, so tracking the expiry date keeps your patient safe. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h7)

question: Where does fluid from the very tip of the tongue first drain into the lymphatic system?

options.A: Submandibular lymph nodes
options.B: Jugulodigastric lymph nodes
options.C: Submental lymph nodes
options.D: Superficial parotid nodes

explanation: The submental nodes sit right under your chin, making them the first stop for lymphatic drainage from the very tip of the tongue. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to involve local leaders when introducing a new immunization campaign?

options.A: Local leaders are legally required to sign off on all nursing licenses
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to buy their own medical supplies
options.C: Local leaders help build trust and encourage community members to participate
options.D: It ensures the village council pays the nurses' salaries

explanation: Community leaders hold influence and respect, making them vital bridges for gaining community acceptance and trust. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: A stroke patient is struggling to button their shirt and brush their teeth. Which specialist should the nurse call first?

options.A: Occupational Therapist
options.B: Physical Therapist
options.C: Respiratory Therapist
options.D: Dietitian

explanation: Spot on! Occupational therapists focus on upper body strength and everyday activities like dressing, bathing, and grooming. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h3)

question: When a patient with a throat infection develops a high fever, tiredness, and swollen neck glands, what do these show?

options.A: Lower airway collapse
options.B: Systemic response to the infection
options.C: Permanent vocal cord damage
options.D: Localized allergic rhinitis

explanation: Spot on! Fever and swollen lymph glands are signs that the whole body's immune system is active and fighting the germs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h3)

question: How should you handle a patient who strongly resists making healthy lifestyle changes?

options.A: Demand immediate compliance because the nurse knows best
options.B: Discontinue all nursing visits until the patient changes their attitude
options.C: Acknowledge the patient's feelings and explore the root cause of hesitation
options.D: Threaten to report the patient to local health authorities

explanation: Commands and threats never work well in nursing. Partner with your patient, listen to their worries, and solve problems together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful public health step for preventing enteric fever?

options.A: Proper sewage disposal systems
options.B: Routine airborne quarantine of households
options.C: Provision of safe drinking water
options.D: Vaccination of high-risk populations

explanation: You nailed it! Since typhoid doesn't travel through the air, locking people in airborne quarantine won't help. Clean water and sanitation are what matter! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h7)

question: A student gets a sudden feeling of dread thinking about an upcoming exam next week. What is the best nursing term for this feeling?

options.A: Agoraphobia
options.B: Anxiety
options.C: Panic attack
options.D: Phobia

explanation: Anxiety is that generalized feeling of worry about future events. Unlike a specific, sudden trigger, it's just your mind working overtime about what's ahead! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is a major cause of family displacement and vulnerability across many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Conflict, banditry, and natural disasters
options.B: Mandatory retirement at age fifty
options.C: Too much funding from foreign donors
options.D: Government laws against farming

explanation: Correct! Insecurity and environmental challenges frequently displace Nigerian families, destroying their homes and traditional support systems. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h3)

question: Which part of the limbic system looks like a seahorse and helps with memory?

options.A: The hippocampus
options.B: The amygdala
options.C: The hypothalamus
options.D: The fornix

explanation: You got it! The hippocampus has a distinct seahorse shape and is essential for helping you form and process new memories. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h2)

question: How do upfront hospital user fees usually affect patients with little income?

options.A: They are given free medications upon arrival
options.B: They are automatically transferred to private suites
options.C: They receive faster treatment than wealthy patients
options.D: They delay seeking care until their condition worsens

explanation: Exactly right. Worrying about money often causes vulnerable patients to stay home until a simple illness turns into a major emergency. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h6)

question: If a patient has a stroke in the left side of the brain, which side of the body will usually show weakness?

options.A: Both sides equally
options.B: The left side
options.C: Only the lower extremities
options.D: The right side

explanation: Remember how nerve pathways cross over in the brainstem? Damage on the left side of the brain affects the right side of the body! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T9#GNS324_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which nursing action is vital for preventing joint stiffness (contractures) in a bedridden patient?

options.A: Performing regular range-of-motion exercises
options.B: Massaging bony prominences with heavy oils
options.C: Keeping the patient flat on their back all day
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent swelling

explanation: Keep those joints moving! Gentle range-of-motion exercises stop muscles and tendons from tightening up and getting stuck in one position. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h8)

question: Beyond treating patients, what is an essential public health task for a nurse on an international disaster team?

options.A: Teaching community members about water purification and disease prevention
options.B: Auditing the international bank accounts of the United Nations
options.C: Negotiating ceasefire agreements between warring military factions
options.D: Purchasing international commercial airline tickets for arriving staff

explanation: Great job! Educating communities on hygiene and preventing disease outbreaks is just as vital as bedside nursing during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h8)

question: What factor most commonly drives teenagers toward dangerous, underground abortion practices?

options.A: Abundant availability of free clinical termination services
options.B: Encouragement from community health committees
options.C: Complete legal protection for all medical procedures
options.D: Strict social stigma, legal restrictions, and lack of safe care access

explanation: Exactly. When judgment, strict laws, and a lack of open support block safe care, desperate teenagers unfortunately turn to risky alternatives. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h5)

question: In a nursing research study, what does the independent variable stand for?

options.A: An unexpected error that ruins the study measurements
options.B: A constant baseline factor that never changes or varies
options.C: The final measured outcome that changes as a result
options.D: The presumed cause or experimental intervention being tested

explanation: Think of the independent variable as the treatment or action the nurse researcher introduces to see what effect it has! [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main reason we group and organize medical supplies in a ward?

options.A: To reduce the total number of items ordered each month
options.B: To prevent medication errors and speed up retrieval
options.C: To make the pharmacy department look neat and tidy
options.D: To ensure patients pay higher fees for their treatments

explanation: A well-organized ward helps you find what you need in a hurry. When every second counts, clear placement keeps your patients safe and cuts down on mistakes. [learn more](GST321_U4_T2#GST321_U4_T2_h2)

question: What happens to chemical indicator strips when they are exposed to the correct sterilization conditions?

options.A: Their weight and density
options.B: Their color
options.C: Their physical length
options.D: Their magnetic polarity

explanation: Spot on! Special dyes in the strip change color to let you know the correct temperature or chemical levels were reached inside the load. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the main goal of nursing data integration?

options.A: Lowering the financial cost of hospital building maintenance
options.B: Replacing all human nurses with automated computer programs
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital beds needed
options.D: Bringing patient information together into a single view

explanation: You've got this! Data integration simply means gathering scattered patient details from different places so you can see the whole picture in one spot. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: A young girl who recently underwent FGM refuses to urinate, looks restless, and has a swollen lower abdomen. What is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Bowel obstruction
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Acute urinary retention

explanation: Well done! Severe pain, swelling, and fear often cause girls to hold their urine, leading to a painfully full bladder and acute urinary retention. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h2)

question: Why do we routinely check a laboring mother's blood pressure?

options.A: To estimate the exact birth weight of the infant
options.B: To detect signs of pre-eclampsia or hemorrhage
options.C: To measure the strength of uterine contractions
options.D: To check how fast the baby's heart is beating

explanation: Spotting dangerous BP spikes (hello, pre-eclampsia!) or sudden drops (bleeding) early lets us protect both mum and baby right away. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h3)

question: What does 'hidden hunger' refer to in public health?

options.A: A temporary shortage of food caused by hidden transport strikes
options.B: A secret eating disorder common among teenagers in urban centers
options.C: A lack of essential micronutrients despite consuming enough daily calories
options.D: The physical sensation of hunger experienced only during night shifts

explanation: Hidden hunger happens when diets fill the stomach with cheap energy sources but lack vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)

question: A patient with heart failure shows sudden weight gain and severe shortness of breath. What does this mean?

options.A: They are severely dehydrated
options.B: Their heart muscle is successfully healing
options.C: They gained sudden muscle mass
options.D: Worsening fluid overload and congestion in the lungs

explanation: That sudden weight gain isn't fat or muscle—it's trapped water! When heart failure worsens, fluid pools up in the body and lungs, making breathing really tough. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h2)

question: Which class of diuretics is known for being the most powerful at removing fluid from the body?

options.A: Potassium-sparing diuretics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Thiazide diuretics
options.D: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors

explanation: Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where a massive amount of sodium is normally reabsorbed, making them very potent. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a health care budget?

options.A: To eliminate all unexpected hospital expenses permanently
options.B: To calculate exact salaries for individual doctors and nurses
options.C: To plan and control financial resources for medical services
options.D: To set the retail prices of medications in the pharmacy

explanation: A health care budget serves as a financial plan to guide how money is spent on patient care services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which drug class is commonly prescribed to cut down stomach acid and heal ulcers?

options.A: Osmotic laxatives
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Proton pump inhibitors
options.D: Anti-platelet agents

explanation: PPIs block the little 'pumps' in your stomach lining that make acid. Less acid means the ulcer finally gets a chance to heal up. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which part of the spinal nerve root sends motor signals away from the spinal cord to your muscles?

options.A: Ventral root
options.B: Dorsal root ganglion
options.C: Ventral ramus
options.D: Dorsal root

explanation: Remember: ventral means front, and the front (ventral) root carries action commands out to your muscles and glands. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h3)

question: Whose responsibility is it to provide safe ergonomic equipment and policies in a hospital?

options.A: Only the individual nurse working night shifts
options.B: The patients admitted to the specific medical ward
options.C: The healthcare institution and facility management
options.D: The federal ministry of finance exclusively

explanation: Well done! Hospitals and facility management have a duty of care to ensure their staff have safe equipment and workspaces. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)

question: What happens when organic matter like blood is left on a surface during disinfection?

options.A: It turns the disinfectant into a complete sterilizing agent
options.B: It neutralizes the chemical and shields microbes from contact
options.C: It helps the disinfectant spread more evenly over tools
options.D: It speeds up the chemical reaction time on the surface
