explanation: Correct! If you mock traditional practices, patients will simply stop telling you what herbal mixtures or remedies they are taking, which can lead to dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why did Nigeria adopt the Expanded Programme on Immunization framework?

options.A: To replace traditional herbal medicine practitioners entirely
options.B: To generate revenue for local government health clinics
options.C: To combat high rates of preventable childhood mortality
options.D: To manage emergency trauma cases from road traffic accidents

explanation: The initiative was localized to address and lower the heavy burden of death caused by infectious childhood diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard community prevention message taught by nurses?

options.A: Attending antenatal clinics for preventive treatment during pregnancy
options.B: Sleeping inside insecticide-treated nets every single night
options.C: Taking high doses of antibiotics to prevent malaria infection
options.D: Clearing stagnant water puddles around residential houses

explanation: Correct! Antibiotics fight bacteria, not malaria parasites. Taking them for malaria is incorrect and only builds drug resistance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why are joint multi-agency simulation drills important before a disaster happens?

options.A: They allow international donors to inspect local hospital buildings
options.B: They build personal trust and working familiarity among different responders
options.C: They eliminate the need for any written emergency response plans
options.D: They guarantee that natural disasters will completely bypass the region

explanation: Training together beforehand ensures that different agencies know each other's styles and work smoothly together when lives are on the line. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h8)

question: Why might wild, erratic vital sign readings with high variability point to a clinical emergency?

options.A: High variability always proves that the sensor equipment is broken
options.B: A steady high reading is always more dangerous than fluctuating numbers
options.C: Unstable fluctuations often signal that homeostatic mechanisms are failing
options.D: Monitors are programmed to sound alarms whenever data is perfectly stable

explanation: When the body's natural balance (homeostasis) starts failing, vital signs bounce all over the place. High variability is often a red flag for a crashing patient! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T5#GNS217_U4_T5_h5)

question: How does adding a little glucose to oral rehydration solution help the body absorb water?

options.A: Glucose creates a thick barrier that stops water from leaving the body
options.B: Glucose binds with sodium to pull water across the gut wall together
options.C: Glucose makes the drink taste sweet so the child will drink more
options.D: Glucose feeds the good bacteria so they can repair the damaged bowel

explanation: It's like a team effort! Sodium and glucose hitch a ride together on the same transport protein. As glucose is absorbed, it pulls sodium and water right along with it into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h3)

question: Who is known as the father of nutrition for his early work on how our bodies use oxygen to burn food for energy?

options.A: James Lind
options.B: Casimir Funk
options.C: Antoine Lavoisier
options.D: Hippocrates

explanation: Correct! Lavoisier used clever chemical experiments to show how respiration and metabolism tie directly into how we process food. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)

question: How can a new home care agency best protect its nurses from safety risks when visiting unfamiliar areas?

options.A: Instructing nurses to never document any clinical findings
options.B: Stopping all home visits after morning hours
options.C: Vetting client locations and utilizing tracking or communication tools
options.D: Requiring families to purchase expensive hospital equipment

explanation: Brilliant! Checking locations beforehand and using check-in tools helps keep field nurses safe and secure. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is the main job of sensory input in our nervous system?

options.A: Sending commands directly to the skeletal muscles
options.B: Detecting changes inside and outside the body
options.C: Producing hormones to regulate blood pressure
options.D: Processing complex thoughts in the spinal cord

explanation: Think of sensory input as your body's early warning system. Receptors pick up information from both your external environment and your insides so you can react! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h1)

question: As a safe nursing habit, why should an arterial line insertion site always be left uncovered by heavy bed linens?

options.A: To allow immediate visual detection of bleeding or disconnection
options.B: To ensure the patient can easily remove the sterile dressing themselves
options.C: To let air circulate so the skin around the puncture site stays dry
options.D: To prevent the electronic blood pressure monitor from overheating

explanation: Safety first! Because arterial pressure is so high, if a line slips out under heavy blankets, a patient could lose a dangerous amount of blood before anyone notices. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T13#GNS125_U3_T13_h4)

question: A patient is prescribed an ipratropium inhaler. Which condition is this medication most likely treating?

options.A: Acute bacterial pneumonia
options.B: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
options.C: Severe hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Ipratropium is a bronchodilator commonly delivered by inhalation to open airways in respiratory conditions like COPD. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic adult illnesses
options.B: To provide free accommodation for teachers
options.C: To replace local hospitals within rural communities
options.D: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff

explanation: The core purpose of the programme is safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of the school population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: What does process data measure in a quality improvement project?

options.A: Patient satisfaction ratings collected after outpatient visits
options.B: The final health status of a patient after discharge
options.C: The total financial budget allocated to a specific ward
options.D: How healthcare services and nursing tasks are delivered

explanation: Process data is all about the *actions* we take. It checks if our day-to-day nursing tasks and clinical steps are actually being done. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h2)
